reading.title: Parts of the head and face
reading.text: Dina reads a simple anatomy guide. The head contains the skull, and the scalp is the skin over it. Temple and crown name areas of the head. The forehead is above the eyebrows. The chin is below the mouth. Dina compares neck and throat, then eye and eyelid. She uses the written guide and an educational model to learn names, rather than to diagnose a person.

reading.title: Dental and hair vocabulary
reading.text: Dina compares a wisdom tooth with a baby tooth in the guide. Enamel covers the tooth crown, and the root extends into its socket. A separate page describes hair. Hairline and part describe its edge and arrangement; strand names a thin length. Beard, mustache, sideburns, stubble and goatee describe facial hair. Dina reads braid as a woven hair arrangement, without making judgments about identity or appearance.
